PullRequest.Title: agentHost: apply pending configuration before MCP startup
PullRequest.Body:
agentHost: apply pending configuration before MCP startup

MCP Start can run before pending plugin configuration reaches the live SDK session. Apply that
configuration before Start and report failures instead of leaving the server in Starting.

- Share configuration refresh between Send and MCP Start, and preserve the SDK session ID.
- Wait for active turns before a Start-triggered refresh. Keep MCP RPCs outside the chat queue.
- Own Start cancellation in AgentSideEffects and pass the token through preparation and startup.
- Publish explicit Start errors without replacing newer requests or authoritative server states.
- Retry failed plugin sync without dropping healthy plugins or skipping identical inputs.
- Add tests for refresh, failure reporting, cancellation, idle waits, and queue independence.

Validation: 1,215 tests passed with one existing pending test. Client type checking, scoped ESLint,
and diff checks passed. A real Code OSS run confirmed Start-triggered refresh and error reporting.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The send/Start critical path calls `retryFailedClientSyncIfNeeded`, the changed method explicitly supplies all client inputs, and the added tests assert that both the failed and healthy plugin are supplied on retry. `AgentPluginManager.syncCustomizations` performs per-input filesystem work and `resolveSyncedCustomization` calls `parsePlugin`, which reads plugin manifests and component directories. Only the typical number/size of installed plugins is uncertain, affecting severity rather than mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem exists/copy/cache-write operations and plugin parsing CPU/allocations for healthy plugin trees
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the total number and size of a client's plugins (N), multiplied by every send or MCP Start while any one plugin remains errored, rather than with only the errored subset (E).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased critical-path latency and repeated filesystem I/O/CPU parsing
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The retry constructed inputs only from errored customizations, so a client with one failed plugin and many healthy siblings retried and reparsed only that failed subset at each message boundary.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: When one customization is in Error, every message boundary and MCP Start now re-syncs the client's entire customization contribution, including all healthy plugins, and reparses every returned plugin directory.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 6845 changes the retry input from `errored.map(item => item.input!)` to the client's complete `client.inputs`; RIGHT line 6723 simultaneously bypasses the identical-input fast path whenever any item is errored, so the full list reaches `syncCustomizations` rather than being deduplicated.
Findings.Title: Retry failed plugins without reprocessing healthy siblings
Findings.Impact: With N client plugins and one persistent/transient failure, each affected prompt or MCP Start incurs O(N) filesystem synchronization and full plugin parsing on its critical path instead of O(number of failed plugins), increasing prompt/start latency and filesystem/CPU load; malformed or unavailable plugins make this recur at every message boundary.
Findings.Evidence: `_refreshSessionConfiguration` awaits `retryFailedClientSyncIfNeeded()` before a send or Start can proceed. The changed retry uses all `client.inputs`; `AgentPluginManager._syncPlugin` performs copy work on uncached/no-nonce inputs, or at minimum an existence check plus cache-file persistence on nonce hits, and every result then runs `parsePlugin`, which reads the manifest, hooks, MCP definitions, skills, agents, and instructions. The new test `Send retries failed sync without dropping healthy plugins` confirms the retry call includes `[pluginDirectory, healthyDirectory]`, not only the failed directory.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the existing healthy client slice while retrying only errored inputs—for example, add a targeted retry/merge path that replaces results by URI instead of making `sync` replace the whole client contribution. This retains healthy siblings without sending them back through plugin synchronization and parsing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a chat message while one client plugin is in an error state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `sendMessage` enters the per-chat queue and awaits `retryFailedClientSyncIfNeeded`, plugin synchronization, resolution/parsing, snapshot comparison, and any required session refresh before calling the SDK send. All of this preparation is on prompt latency's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize or validate each plugin cache entry, persist cache metadata, and parse plugin manifests/components.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After the diff, N sync operations for every plugin contributed by a client whenever at least one is errored; previously E operations for only the errored subset, where E is commonly 1 and N may include many healthy plugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only errored inputs were re-synchronized and parsed on a message-boundary retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All syncs and subsequent plugin parses must complete before the prompt reaches the SDK.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the user prompt to the Copilot SDK session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK send per prompt after preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK send occurred, but healthy sibling plugins were not reprocessed during failed-plugin retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts the actual turn only after configuration preparation completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total client-contributed plugins and their manifest/component tree sizes, multiplied by prompts while any customization remains errored.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Messages are serialized per chat. Within one client sync, all N plugin inputs are synchronized in parallel (serialized only by plugin URI); clients containing errors are retried sequentially. The parallel fan-out does not reduce aggregate filesystem/parsing work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful healthy plugins may hit the nonce materialization cache, but each retry still checks the directory, persists the shared cache metadata, and reparses the plugin tree; inputs without a nonce can be recopied. Error states are deliberately retried at every message boundary, so persistent failures receive no negative-cache/backoff behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed full-input array, send call path, filesystem implementation, parser, and new test assertions establish the mechanism and O(N) cardinality directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The installed plugin count and tree sizes vary by user, but a single unavailable or malformed plugin is a realistic persistent trigger; exact added milliseconds are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated filesystem and parsing work: the diff expands each retry from the failed subset to every healthy sibling on the prompt critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start an MCP server with pending plugin configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MCP Start is first prepared in the per-chat queue. It awaits failed-plugin retry, snapshot/enablement comparison, and—when configuration changed—SDK disconnect and session resume; after preparation leaves the chat queue, the requested server's Start RPC must complete. During an active turn, refresh waits for idle and cancellation can end the caller wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry plugin materialization and parse all contributed plugin trees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N plugin sync/parse operations if any client plugin is errored, versus E failed-plugin operations before this diff's full-input retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: MCP Start did not prepare session configuration; the pre-existing message retry path processed only errored inputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks configuration preparation and therefore delays server Start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Disconnect the old Copilot SDK session and resume/create the configured replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when no refresh reason exists; otherwise one SDK disconnect and one resume/create operation for the addressed session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Start directly targeted the current runtime and did not refresh pending configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to apply pending configuration before Start; Start waits for replacement runtime registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke `session.rpc.mcp.startServer` for the resolved server name.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK MCP Start RPC per effective Start request; duplicate same-server requests cancel the older host request, although an already-running SDK operation may finish.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Start RPC was issued directly against the current session without configuration preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Start action completes only when this RPC settles; it is intentionally outside the chat queue.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number/size of client plugins for retry work; one session restart and one Start RPC per request that observes pending configuration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Preparation is serialized per chat. The MCP Start RPC runs outside the chat queue and is sequenced per server name, so different server RPCs can proceed concurrently; AgentSideEffects supersedes and cancels duplicate starts for the same session/server.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Preparation uses the same plugin cache behavior as sends. Snapshot data is rebuilt rather than memoized, while customization enablement session initialization is internally reusable. A pending configuration change causes one refreshed live SDK runtime; unchanged configuration avoids disconnect/resume.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: queue placement, idle handling, refresh boundaries, per-server sequencing, and test gates explicitly establish ordering and concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session restart and plugin synchronization duration depend on runtime and plugin size. The refresh itself is intentional; the reported regression is specifically reprocessing healthy siblings.
Scenarios.Verdict: The preparation/restart behavior is intentional and bounded, but its full-client failed-plugin retry shares the reported O(N) regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel or stop an MCP Start during configuration preparation or SDK startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A Stop first waits for already-queued chat preparation for that session, then invokes the current runtime's Stop operation. If a same-server Start RPC is already running, the per-server lifecycle sequencer orders Stop after it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the SDK MCP server Stop RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK MCP Stop RPC per Stop request when a live control chat exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Stop RPC occurred immediately against the currently found runtime; the diff adds only an in-process queue barrier so it reaches a replacement runtime after refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Stop completion waits for the RPC and for any preceding same-server lifecycle operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user Stop request and at most the preceding preparation/replacement operation for that chat; no collection fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The chat barrier serializes Stop behind configuration preparation, but MCP RPCs for different server names remain independent. Same-session/server Start cancellation is coalesced by the AgentSideEffects map.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stop performs no plugin refresh. It resolves the live/backing session from in-memory maps. Cancellation suppresses superseded Start failure publication; no retained cancellation entry remains after settlement or disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the empty chat-queue barrier and per-server sequencer are explicit and covered by disconnect/resume tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A barrier can inherit latency from an in-progress configuration refresh, but that ordering is required to avoid targeting the retiring runtime and does not introduce additional boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance finding: cancellation sources are cleaned up, queue/RPC ordering is bounded, and cross-server/chat work remains independent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Re-publish an unchanged client customization list containing one failed plugin
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A client re-publishing customizations (for example after navigating away and back) awaits the controller sync and its filesystem/parser work before the refreshed customization result settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate/materialize and reparse the entire client customization list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N plugin syncs/parses for an identical publication when one item is errored; previously zero because identical inputs always returned the existing settled sync.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical input lists were deduplicated regardless of an existing error state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays customization publication/navigation-associated refresh and adds filesystem load.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total plugins in the republished client contribution and number of identical re-publications while an error persists.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All plugin inputs for that client fan out concurrently through the plugin manager, with per-URI sequencing; there is no grouping that avoids healthy inputs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Identical healthy customization publications still hit the in-memory equality fast path. If any one customization is errored, the diff intentionally bypasses that fast path and performs a full sync; nonce hits avoid copying but not existence checks, cache persistence, or reparsing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed equality guard directly changes an identical errored input from no-op to full synchronization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Navigation/republication frequency and plugin counts vary; this is the same root cause and fix as the submitted full-client retry finding, so it is not reported separately.
Scenarios.Verdict: Confirms the submitted repeated-work mechanism but is not a distinct finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files. One medium-severity repeated-work regression was submitted: failed-plugin recovery now re-synchronizes and reparses every healthy sibling on send/Start and identical re-publication paths. MCP refresh, idle waiting, cancellation ownership, failure publication, and Stop ordering were also traced; their boundary counts and lifecycles are bounded and did not yield additional high-confidence performance issues.
